name: POST /api/sla/alerts/acknowledge - Acknowledge my SLA alerts for a lead
description: Acknowledges every SLA alert addressed to the CALLING user for one lead - the manager equivalent of clearing a notification once they have looked at it. A command against existing rows rather than the creation of a resource, so it answers 200 (MUST-54). Scoped to the caller's own alerts BY DESIGN: the recipient comes from the bearer token, never from the body, so one manager cannot silence an escalation addressed to another. That is why the endpoint is keyed on lead_id rather than an alert id - a breach raises one row per manager, and the caller acknowledges their own. Acknowledging sets state to acknowledged and stamps acknowledged_at, which takes the lead off that manager's queue WITHOUT clearing the breach on the lead itself: a missed deadline is a historical fact, and letting an acknowledgement erase it would make the compliance number meaningless. IDEMPOTENT: a second call reports already_acknowledged:true and changes nothing. EXPECT acknowledged:0 IN A CLEAN QA RUN, and that is the CORRECT contract, not a failure - alerts are raised only by the monitoring sweep for a lead that is at_risk or breached, and no API can make a response clock expire (it would require waiting out the whole window), so a freshly captured lead inside its window has nothing to acknowledge. The behaviour with real alerts present is covered by server/tests/integration/slaAlert.test.ts, which places a clock in the past directly - something the application deliberately cannot do. QA: depends on register, login, a captured lead and a sweep; lead_id comes from the capture's captured id.

transitions.notes: The row is written first and the outbound notification attempted second, so an alert is never lost because the gateway was briefly unreachable. A pending alert is already visible in-app.
Set once the retry budget is exhausted. The row remains readable in-app - a failed OUTBOUND send must not mean a silent escalation.
The recipient has seen it. Stamps acknowledged_at and acknowledged_by_user_id. Does NOT clear leads.sla_breached - the breach is a historical fact.
A manager who saw the alert in-app can acknowledge it even though the outbound send never landed.

testCases.name: Acknowledge my alerts for the captured lead
Reject a lead_id that is not a UUID

errorCases.when: lead_id is absent or not a well-formed UUID
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
no lead exists with the supplied lead_id
